attacks.name: PD-40 Sticky Stop: does a human Stop between asks durably protect the reviewer?
attacks.instrument: tests/kits/wp1-sticky-stop, arm B (no latch) with arm A (latch) as control; fresh DSH_HOME per arm
attacks.expectation: if the claim holds, the Stop writes a durable marker and the next review ask wakes nobody
attacks.observed: ARM B: 4/4 PASS. No marker is written (markers=[] at both points), the Stop returns through the coordinator-undefined branch, nothing claims durable protection (stopClaims.hits=[]), and after ONE ordinary human re-engagement turn the next review ask ACTIVATES the reviewer at the model (wakes 0->1, wakeId review-wake:…:1:a6wake%3Av1%3A1%3A4b574e25, markersAfter=[]). ARM A control: 6/6 PASS — the latch path writes exactly one marker (stopped-a525fde5.json, pathOk/keyOk/contentOk true), a machine relay and a machine work delivery do not clear it (wakes 1->1 both), the marker survives SIGKILL + cold boot byte-identical, and after cold boot a NEW review leg for the same reviewer is suppressed (legs 1->2, wakes 1->1).
durableRows: wp1-armB/b3-no-marker.json: markers=[] wakeRows=[] returnValue.observed=inferred-false why=root.ts:2755-2762 returns false when alpha6WakeBySession has no coordinator
wp1-armB/b4-next-wake.json: wakesBefore=0 wakesAfter=1 requestId=ctrl-048vrp70maj6r81kenot516i markersAfter=[] note=“the disclosed limit, observed”
wp1-armA/wp1 summary: A1 PASS intent=wake-a525fde5.json; A3 PASS markers=[stopped-a525fde5.json]
attacks.bound: The marker is latch-scoped and has no session-scoped durability; nothing on this tree changes that conclusion (the writer is still gated on `coordinator === undefined`). RELEASE-NOTES §4.7 and register PD-40 already carry this disclosure, so the defect does not falsify a promise the notes make — it falsifies any reading of “Sticky Stop” as session-scoped protection.

attacks.name: Alpha.6 default-off zero regression, then opt-in approvals + Goals
attacks.instrument: host-free structural probes (ATTACK C in the adjudicator suite) + the A5-only pd33 world (alpha6ReviewRouting absent) + the joint kit (alpha6-on) twice
attacks.expectation: with the opt-in absent nothing Alpha.6 runs and Alpha.5 behaviour is unchanged; with the opt-in on, approvals and Goals both work in two fresh worlds
attacks.observed: STRUCTURE: createAlpha6RootWiring(false|undefined|1) returns {mode:'legacy'} without invoking the composition thunk (0 invocations), and controlRequestNotification with the opt-in absent keeps the Alpha.5 Leader notifier; opt-in present without a wake seam refuses instead of falling back to the Leader. A6-ON: joint 11/11 PASS twice, detail agreement true (approvals J05, Goals J07, identity J06, relay refusal J08). A6-OFF: pd33 16/19 — three cases FAIL because every governed `bash` call is refused with `A5_NATIVE_ADMISSION_UNAVAILABLE: the Team admission edge is not published for this agent, so this native bash call cannot be decided or consumed; refusing instead of executing an unapproved native call` (member-a-io-chain: none-errored + facts-per-tool factless=[bash]; member-a-authorization: out-of-bounds-command-zero-side-effect; shell-write-boundary: guard-admits-the-spawn + os-profile-stops-the-write).
durableRows: attacks/c2b-adv-attack.log: C1 legacy without thunk invocation; C2 Alpha.5 notifier preserved
runs/boot01/run-record.json: overall=FAIL, 3 failing cases, clause detail quoted above
attacks.bound: The structural default-off gate is proven. The measured consequence of default-off is NOT indistinguishable from the Alpha.5 baseline the pd33 instrument recorded on a2e0df3c9 (19/19): the governed bash now refuses before execution on a composition that does not mount the plane takeover. Both compositions that passed (A1, joint) set the takeover explicitly. Whether this is instrument staleness (the world predates #730's native admission slot) or a default-path product regression is NOT decidable from my runs; I did not find a shipped Alpha.5-only composition that mounts the takeover.

adjudicator_suite.note: adjudicator-written probe, left uncommitted in the adjudication worktree; includes two positive controls for #738 (RUNNING and SETTLED owners)

signedClaims: On the routes measured, the compiled effective lane never exceeds MemberCeiling(member) ∩ ToolRestriction(member,tool); refusals are typed and precede execution (0 bytes, 0 consumptions, 0 execution results).

A durable PENDING leg is the subject of validity: ARCHIVED/DISPOSED owners, mismatched Blueprint hash or revision, missing legs, decided legs, wrong authority generation and non-current ordinals are all refused; RUNNING (ordinary path) and SETTLED owners both pass.
The Alpha.6 opt-in is a structural gate: absent/false does not invoke the composition thunk and keeps the Alpha.5 Leader notifier.
With the opt-in on, one tarball serves approvals and Goals end to end: joint 11/11 twice with detail agreement.
The accepted-but-not-claimed window is counted (pendingControlCount=1), readable by id and resolvable by an operator allow.
A request decided before the crash is terminally abandoned with a typed fact, executes nothing, is not revived, and a late allow is refused with CONTROL_REQUEST_ABANDONED.
The packed tree and the installed tree are identical; tarball sha256 7a1d754c… reproduced independently; version 0.1.6.
PD-40 is real and is disclosed in RELEASE-NOTES §4.7: a human Stop between asks is latch-scoped, not session-scoped.
refusedClaims: R1 “With alpha6ReviewRouting off, Alpha.5 behaviour is unchanged (zero regression).” Refused: the A5-only pd33 world reddens 3/19 on governed bash with A5_NATIVE_ADMISSION_UNAVAILABLE. Instrument staleness vs product regression is not decided here.

R2 “PD-42's A1 is closed: an approved bash call is bounded by the compiled ceiling.” Refused: no instrument I ran measures allow → body executes → out-of-lane target; A1's approval arm denies and joint's bash is in-lane.
R3 “A human Stop between asks protects the reviewer durably (Sticky Stop).” Refused: PD-40 reproduced; no marker on the no-latch path, next ask wakes the reviewer.
R4 “Every accepted review wake is delivered or decidable.” Refused (and already withdrawn by #740 §5): abandoned-terminal is a third outcome.
R5 “PD-43 / RELEASE-NOTES §4.10 accurately describe this tree.” Refused: both still say the lifecycle gate is OPEN although #738 on this SHA fixes it.
R6 “The operator re-issue path works.” Not measured: I exercised resolve-by-id of the stranded request, not re-issue of a new ask.

disclosures.subject: A5-only composition refuses governed bash after #730/#739
disclosures.detail: pd33 (alpha6ReviewRouting absent, memberPresetId=a5sf-governed-member, plane takeover NOT mounted) has 16/19 cases PASS; the 3 failures are all the same refusal: A5_NATIVE_ADMISSION_UNAVAILABLE from packages/runtime/src/plugin/live/native-tool-admission.mjs (the plane never published admitNative for that Agent). The recorded pd33 pair on a2e0df3c9 was 19/19. The two compositions that pass here (A1, joint) set the plane takeover explicitly. Consequence: the Alpha.5 Preview's bash row is not reproducible on the composition its own evidence was recorded on. Owner must decide whether the shipped A5-only path is required to work without the takeover (then this is a real regression), or whether every supported composition now must mount it (then the pd33 instrument is stale and must be updated before it can carry a zero-regression claim).

disclosures.subject: Documentation stale on the fixed lifecycle gate
disclosures.detail: PRODUCT-DEBT-REGISTER PD-43 row says OPEN — not fixed, and RELEASE-NOTES §4.10 still calls it open, while #738 (76293c79f, on this SHA) fixes exactly that gate and changed no docs. My A2 measurements (8/8 refusals plus the 31-test suite) corroborate the code, not the prose.

disclosures.subject: wp1 arm A first launch aborted, reported run is the completed rerun
disclosures.detail: The first wp1 arm A launch was detached with a shell `&` and died with its parent shell after four log lines; it produced no verdict and is not cited. The reported arm A run is a clean rerun that completed 6/6 PASS. No product behaviour is inferred from the aborted attempt.

disclosures.subject: Packaging driver gap, adjudication-side workaround
disclosures.detail: `--phase install --tarball <prebuilt>` cannot evaluate INST-6 (reused-tarball mode omits treeDigest). I ran `--phase all` so the driver packed and hashed its own tree, and independently recomputed the tarball sha256 and internal version.

disclosures.subject: Adjudicator test file is uncommitted
disclosures.detail: packages/runtime/test/c2b-adv-attack-20261116.test.ts exists only in .worktrees/c2b-cand3 (untracked). It is probe code, not product code; the record cites it by path and log.

disclosures.subject: PD-39 promise wording
disclosures.detail: The stranded window is now countable and resolvable (measured), but “delivered” is not what I measured, and the terminal-abandonment trigger (decision before crash) is real. The §5 narrow wording is the only one this record supports.

verdict: NOT PASS (candidate claim not eligible from this record)
verdictBasis: Two independent reasons: (1) A4 is not established — the default-off Alpha.5 world reddens on governed bash; (2) PD-40 is reproduced. The invariant, approval-validity, promise-boundary and packaging claims measured here do survive, with the explicit bounds recorded in each attack.
